---
title: Author name particles
author:
  - Charles de Gaulle
  - name:
      given: Frank S.
      family: Boer
      non-dropping-particle: de
  - given: Ludwig
    family: Beethoven
    non-dropping-particle: van
  - Johannes van der Waals
  - Plato
  - name:
      literal: Johann Wolfgang von Goethe
      given: J. W.
  - name:
      literal: Jean de La Fontaine
      dropping-particle: de
  - name:
      given: Alexander
      family: Humboldt
      dropping-particle: von
  - name:
      literal: Vincent van Gogh
      family: van Gogh
  - name:
      family: van den Bosch
format:
  html: default
  jats: default
_quarto:
  tests:
    html:
      ensureFileRegexMatches:
        - ['<p>Charles de Gaulle\s*</p>', '<p>Frank S\. de Boer\s*</p>', '<p>Ludwig van Beethoven\s*</p>', '<p>Alexander von Humboldt\s*</p>', '<p>Johannes van der Waals\s*</p>', '<p>Plato\s*</p>']
        - ['<p>Frank S\. Boer\s*</p>', '<p>Ludwig Beethoven\s*</p>', '<p>Alexander Humboldt\s*</p>']
    jats:
      ensureFileRegexMatches:
        - ['<given-names>Alexander von</given-names>', '<surname>de Gaulle</surname>', '<surname>de Boer</surname>', '<surname>van Beethoven</surname>', '<surname>van der Waals</surname>', '<surname>Plato</surname>', '<surname>von Goethe</surname>', '<given-names>J\. W\.</given-names>', '<surname>La Fontaine</surname>', '<given-names>Jean de</given-names>', '<surname>van Gogh</surname>', '<surname>van den Bosch</surname>']
        - ['<surname>Gaulle</surname>', '<surname>Boer</surname>', '<surname>Beethoven</surname>', '<surname>Waals</surname>', 'J\. W\.Johann', '<given-names>Johann Wolfgang</given-names>', '<surname>de La Fontaine</surname>', 'van van Gogh', 'van den van den Bosch']
---

Particles in author names must survive author normalization.

- `Charles de Gaulle` is a plain string: Pandoc's BibTeX parse finds the particle `de`.
- `Frank S. de Boer` is a `name:` table with an explicit `non-dropping-particle`.
- `Ludwig van Beethoven` uses flat `given`, `family` and `non-dropping-particle` fields.
- `Johannes van der Waals` is a string with a multi-word particle.
- `Plato` is a single-word string: no particle, no stray spaces.
- `Johann Wolfgang von Goethe` has a literal plus a written `given`, which must survive the parse.
- `Jean de La Fontaine` has a literal plus an explicit particle, which wins over the parse.
- `Alexander von Humboldt` has an explicit `dropping-particle`: the title block shows it, and JATS keeps it with the given names.
- `Vincent van Gogh` has a literal plus a written `family` that already holds the particle, which must not be added twice.
- `van den Bosch` is a written `family` alone, holding its particle: nothing is added to it.
